new_groups.label: The King's speech of October 1775
new_groups.definition: Printings of George III's speech opening the session of Parliament in October 1775, which the American papers printed from January 1776. The printings date the speech differently: the 26th in one, the 27th in another.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Siege of Quebec
new_groups.definition: Reports of the American siege of Quebec in the 1776 papers: Montgomery's letter calling on Carleton to surrender (December 1775), the account of the failed assault of 31 December, and a camp letter of 6 April 1776. Contains those three groups; the wider coverage is not included.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Montgomery's letter to Carleton
new_groups.definition: Printings of General Montgomery's letter to Governor Carleton from before Quebec, dated December 1775, calling on him to surrender the town.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Failed assault on Quebec
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Philadelphia report (25 January 1776) of the unsuccessful attempt to take Quebec by storm on 31 December 1775.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Letter from the camp before Quebec
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from the American camp before Quebec, dated 6 April 1776, on the batteries and the want of men. It circulated in two versions.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Boston evacuated
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from headquarters at Cambridge, 19 March 1776, reporting that the British army left Boston on 17 March.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Congress opens the ports
new_groups.definition: Printings of Congress's resolutions of 6 April 1776 opening American ports to trade with all countries not under the British crown.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Hopkins's report from New Providence
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of Commodore Esek Hopkins's letter of 9 April 1776 to the President of Congress, on the fleet's expedition to New Providence in the Bahamas.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A Dublin paper: British force coming
new_groups.definition: Printings of news brought to Philadelphia in May 1776 by a passenger from Europe with a Dublin paper of 2 March: that a large naval force was coming to America and was ordered to sail on 10 April, followed by London paragraphs from that paper. new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Ethan Allen at Cork
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from Cork (January 1776) on the gifts collected for Colonel Ethan Allen and his fellow prisoners in the Solebay, with Allen's note of thanks.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Rhode Island renounces allegiance

dispositions_summary.method: The 310 matched families first printed in 1776 that reach 4 or more newspapers were split into 1,219 single printed items by work/story_items.py (each printing's opening, looked for on all 2,319 pages of 1776 in both transcriptions). The 188 items printed in 7 or more newspapers (101 distinct documents or reports) were read; 28 were admitted as 22 stories, and phrase searches (phrase_patterns.json) confirmed their printings.
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: Every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs. Items in 7 or 8 newspapers were chosen to cover the months from January to November and the main kinds of news: congressional and colonial documents, British documents, war reports and letters. One item a paper printed again later counts as a separate printing.
